newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe bourse mixed to softer on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe bourse mixed to softer on profit-taking.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial stocks lost more than 200 points on Monday as a spate of profit-taking, mainly in heavyweight counters, put brakes to the local bourse's two-month bullrun.
The key 57-share industrial index fell 273.14 points, or 2.6 percent, to close at 10,018.37.
"Sellers have come out in full force and we expect the correction to continue for a week or two. I don't see it continuing for too long," one broker said.
"At the moment it's a mixed market with second liners appearing firm while blue chips are leading the losers," he added.

Among the day's losers, clothing retailer Edgars slid 400 cents to 4,700, bankers Barclays dropped 300 cents to 3,300, cigarette manufacturer Rothmans fell 200 cents to 6,300 while bankers FMB and blue-chip beverages and supermarkets conglomerate Delta lost 100 cents each to 6,000 and 4,400 respectively.

Soft drinks manufacturer Schweppes shed 40 cents to 300, as did tyre company NTS to 560, tobacco firm TSL traded 20 cents down at 700, textiler Spinweave was 15 cents off at 110 while clothing and furniture retailer Tedco at 1,140 and transport group Clan at 560 both lost 10 cents.

Against the trend, department stores Haddon and Sly rose 50 cents to 650, construction firm J and F climbed 40 cents to 260, Alloys traded 25 cents higher at 775, house appliances-maker Capri added 20 cents to 150, glass firm PG put on 15 cents to 600 while builders Mash and engineering group Gullivers were each 10 cents up at 260 and 250 respectively.
Minings were mixed in lacklustre trade with gold producer Ashanti leaping 700 cents up to 9,200 while nickel miner Bindura shed 10 cents to 850 and Wankie Colliery dropped 25 cents to 550.
The seven-counter mining index lost 25.08 points to end at 1,091.22.
